jobs.title: HighRadius Cash Application Consultant, Associate
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

We are looking for a HighRadius Cash Application Consultant for our rapidly growing national HighRadius practice. This dynamic team is a part of our overall Finance Transformation solution focused on “modernizing the office of the CFO.” This is an ideal opportunity for someone who is looking for an entrepreneurial opportunity within the security of a well-established firm. This position will be directly involved with relationship management and onsite client projects.

As our HighRadius Cash Application Implementation Consultant, you will be able to draw from your experience and knowledge to help clients improve their business by providing services such as HighRadius Cash Application Implementations, Process Improvement, Financial Transformation, Procedure Design and Optimization, etc. This practice line is exciting, growing and offers tremendous career opportunity.
Key Responsibilities:
- Consulting with clients’ accounting, financial, operational and other management personnel to improve their businesses.
- Lead HighRadius Cash Application implementation projects, assess, troubleshoot/test during the implementation cycle.
- Configure, test and debug the HighRadius Cash Application solution.
- Collaborate with functional leads, technical teams, product management, and QA to deploy solutions rapidly.
- Train and advise clients in the leading use of HighRadius products to fit their specific needs.
- Cross train on additional HighRadius modules to ensure comprehensive understanding and ability to diversify implementation capabilities.
- Train and mentor staff/project team.
- All engagements require process analysis/optimization, documentation, project management skills and the ability to work in collaborative teams.
- Participate in the sales process.

Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, accounting or related field.
- Minimum 1 years of end-to-end HighRadius Cash Application implementation experience.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Consulting or Professional Services firm experience is preferred with previous pre-sales/sales experience.
- Understanding and demonstrated experience with working with multiple clients.
- Corporate or industry accounting experience.
- Previous experience with operational process reviews and basic internal control requirements
- Ability to anticipate and address client concerns and issues.
- Fast learner, ability to break complex issues into project steps and problem solve.
- Ability to facilitate clients, and project teams, at all levels of the organization.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong data assimilation and organization skills.
- Strong self-direction and team working skills.
- Experience working with teams in the US.
- Understanding and demonstrated experience with working with multiple clients

jobs.description:

RSM's Management Consulting - Finance Performance practice provides strategic advisory to our clients to enhance the overall effectiveness and efficiency of the Finance function. As a Management Consulting Senior Associate in the Finance Performance practice, you will collaborate with businesses across various industries, working with a team to ensure the timely, budget-compliant, and client-focused delivery of engagements. Engaging in multiple projects annually, you will contribute to several aspects of each engagement, fostering a comprehensive and fulfilling work experience. Our supportive and respectful team environment empowers our consultants to excel, advancing their careers and professional skills.

Responsibilities
- Project Execution: Assist in optimizing all elements of the finance organization, including finance assessment, target operating model definition, business process improvement, enterprise transformation, and finance technology enablement and deployment.
- Finance Function Expertise: Demonstrate an understanding of finance and accounting functions and the people, processes, and technology components that support them, such as Procure to Pay, Order to Cash, Source to Report, Acquire to Retire, and Forecasting & Planning.
- Quality Delivery: Deliver high-quality work within expected timeframes, scope, budgets, and client expectations.
- Digital Delivery: Leveraging digital skillsets – e.g. experience with visualization tools like PowerBI, Tableau as well as automation technologies such as Alteryx, continue to focus on modernizing our service delivery model within Management Consulting through the digitization of our service offerings.
- Project Monitoring: Assist with the monitoring of project progress, management of risk, and ensure project teams and clients are informed about key milestones, engagement progress, and expected outcomes.
- Business Development: Participate in internal and external business development activities and networking.
- Cross-Selling: Understand firm capabilities across lines of business to identify cross-selling opportunities.
- Industry Research: Identify industry focus areas, assist with industry research, and support prospect and existing client targeting activities.
- Project Execution: Contribute to the execution of individual projects to completion, identifying opportunities and solutions to client challenges.
- Service Development: Assist in developing new service offerings, innovative solutions, and deliverables for the rapidly changing finance environment and market.
- Mentorship: Effectively manage, coach, and develop junior resource s and peers by providing timely and actionable feedback, as well as recruitment and retention efforts.
- Communication: Communicate effectively both internally and externally with client employees, C-suite executives and/or private equity partners to develop and foster client relationships.

Basic Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Technology or other related discipline
- Minimum 2 years’ experience working in a large organization, professional services firm or CPA firm.
- Ability to demonstrate knowledge in advising Finance organizations on the above business processes.
- Experience in at least one of the following focus areas: - Finance Transformation
- Business Process Improvement
- Shared Services
- Technology Enablement

- Excellent critical thinking skills and ability to solve complex business problems through fact gathering, business process mapping, and data analysis.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-evolving work environment and deal effectively with ambiguity.
- Must be a team player; demonstrate attention to detail and problem-solving skills; able to effectively work independently and in a team environment.
- Excellent verbal and written communication, project management, and organizational skills.
- Proficiency in MS Word, MS PowerPoint, MS Project, MS Visio, MS Teams, MS Outlook, OneDrive, LucidCharts, Smartsheet
- Ability to travel up to 30%

Preferred Qualifications:
- Functional understanding of financial systems, business processes, and concepts in process redesign
- Digital experience and skillsets with enabling tools such as PowerBI, Alteryx, SQL Server, VBA, Python etc.
- Experience developing and delivering proposals to include scope, approach, timeline, team structure, and fees.
- Experience serving clients across multiple industries.
- Depth of experience in specific industries and sectors, specifically TMT (Technology, SaaS, Media), Real Estate and Construction, Manufacturing, Insurance and Banking
- Industry or professional focused certification (Six Sigma / PMP / CPA a plus)
- MBA or other equivalent or relevant graduate degree

At RSM, we offer a competitive benefits and compensation package for all our people. We offer flexibility in your schedule, empowering you to balance life’s demands, while also maintaining your ability to serve clients. Learn more about our total rewards at https://rsmus.com/careers/working-at-rsm/benefits .

jobs.title: Manager, Treasury Consultant – Global Treasury Practice
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

Treasury Consulting Professionals – Global Treasury Practice
We are seeking Treasury Consulting professionals across multiple experience levels and areas of specialization to join our rapidly growing Global Treasury Practice. Opportunities may range from Senior Associate to Manager level and are available for candidates with expertise in Treasury Technology, Treasury Operations and Advisory, Finance Transformation, and Treasury within Financial Services organizations.

Our Treasury Practice is part of our broader Finance Transformation solution focused on modernizing the Office of the CFO. This is an exceptional opportunity for professionals seeking an entrepreneurial environment within the stability and resources of a well-established global firm. Team members work directly with clients, helping them transform treasury organizations, optimize processes, implement technology solutions, and improve financial performance.
We are looking for professionals with experience in one or more of the following areas:
- Treasury Management System (TMS) implementations and optimization

- Treasury technology strategy and digital transformation

- Treasury operations and process improvement

- Cash and liquidity management

- Bank connectivity and payments transformation

- Cash forecasting and working capital optimization

- Risk management, including FX, interest rate, and commodity exposures

- In-house banking and treasury centralization initiatives

- Treasury controls, governance, and policy development

- Treasury operating model design

- Financial services treasury functions, including liquidity management, funding, capital management, balance sheet management, ALM, regulatory reporting, and treasury risk management

-
Finance transformation and broader CFO organization initiatives

As part of our Treasury Practice, you will leverage your experience and expertise to help clients improve business performance through technology enablement, process transformation, organizational design, and treasury best practices. This practice continues to experience significant growth and offers outstanding career development opportunities both domestically and internationally.

Key Responsibilities
Responsibilities will vary based on experience level and specialization but may include:
- Advise treasury, finance, accounting, and operational leaders on treasury transformation initiatives and leading practices.

- Lead or support Treasury Management System implementations, upgrades, assessments, and optimization projects.

- Evaluate current-state treasury processes and design future-state operating models and solutions.

- Gather business requirements, facilitate workshops, and develop functional and technical specifications.

- Assess, troubleshoot, test, and support treasury technology solutions throughout implementation lifecycles.

- Train and advise clients on the effective use of treasury systems and related technologies.

- Support treasury process improvement initiatives across cash management, liquidity, forecasting, payments, investments, debt, and risk management activities.

- Assist clients with treasury policy development, governance frameworks, controls, and operating procedures.

- Contribute to finance transformation, automation, and digital treasury initiatives.

- Participate in business development, proposal development, pre-sales activities, and client relationship management.

- Develop project plans, manage project workstreams, and coordinate cross-functional stakeholders.

- Mentor and develop junior staff and project team members.

- Build and maintain strong client relationships while delivering high-quality project outcomes.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field.

- Relevant experience in treasury consulting, treasury operations, treasury technology, financial services treasury, banking, or finance transformation.

- Experience in one or more treasury disciplines, including treasury technology, cash management, liquidity management, forecasting, payments, bank relationship management, debt and investments, treasury risk management, or treasury operations.

- Experience with Treasury Management Systems and treasury-related technologies, including but not limited to Kyriba, FIS, Trovata, SAP Treasury, GTreasury, Reval, or similar platforms.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.

- Ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, treasury teams, finance organizations, and technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience implementing, configuring, optimizing, or supporting treasury technology platforms.

- Certifications in Kyriba, FIS, SAP Treasury, or other treasury technologies.

- Corporate treasury experience within large multinational organizations.

- Treasury experience within banking, financial institutions, asset management, insurance, fintech, or other financial services organizations.

- Consulting or professional services experience, including client-facing project delivery.

- Experience supporting treasury transformation, finance transformation, or ERP-enabled treasury initiatives.

- Knowledge of cash management, liquidity management, forecasting, payments, bank connectivity, SWIFT, treasury accounting, debt management, investments, and risk management.

- Understanding of treasury controls, governance, compliance, and regulatory requirements.

- Experience working with multiple clients and managing concurrent project engagements.

- Demonstrated ability to identify client needs, develop solutions, and build trusted advisor relationships.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including workshop facilitation and executive presentations.

- Ability to break down complex business and technology challenges into actionable project plans and solutions.

- Strong data analysis, organization, and documentation skills.

- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within cross-functional and global teams.

Why Join Our Treasury Practice
Our Treasury Practice combines deep functional treasury expertise with leading treasury technology capabilities to help organizations modernize and optimize their treasury operations. Team members have the opportunity to work on strategic initiatives across a broad range of industries, including corporate treasury and financial services, while developing expertise in both business transformation and technology-enabled solutions.
Whether your background is in treasury technology, treasury operations, treasury advisory, financial services treasury, or consulting, we welcome professionals who are passionate about helping clients solve complex treasury challenges and drive meaningful business outcomes.

jobs.title: Director, Life Sciences ERP Risk Transformation Advisory
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSMs Business Application Risk Solutions practice specializes in managing governance, risk, security, data, and compliance across the full lifecycle of core business applications—from implementation through steady-state operations.  We help organizations de‑risk transformations through independent verification and validations (IV&Vs), or through regulatory requirements system integrity solutions including FDA/GxP/CSA validation and system integration readiness, program risk management, and rigorous data quality validation and analytics. We design and manage integrated and scalable compliant application security solutions. We unlock the power of business applications, enabling automation to manage operational and regulatory compliance risk, or implementing intelligent controls, compliance analytics, and business application GRC solutions.

The Life Sciences ERP Risk Transformation Advisory Director will serve as a strategic growth leader within RSM's Business Application Risk Solutions practice, focused on expanding market presence and driving revenue across the life sciences sector.

This individual will build and grow client relationships, identify and pursue new business opportunities, and serve as a trusted advisor guiding organizations through complex ERP-enabled transformations while addressing FDA, GxP, CSA, validation, compliance, and system integrity requirements.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of regulatory requirements associated with ERP implementations and can confidently articulate validation, compliance, and risk management considerations during executive-level conversations. While deep technical expertise is not required, this individual must be able to connect regulatory requirements to business outcomes and collaborate effectively with technical specialists responsible for solution delivery.

Significant experience supporting large-scale ERP implementations, including SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or Microsoft Dynamics environments, is critical.

Business Development & Growth Leadership
- Drive revenue growth by identifying, developing, and closing new business opportunities across the life sciences marketplace.
- Build and maintain executive-level relationships with prospects, clients, technology alliance partners, and industry stakeholders.
- Lead sales pursuits from opportunity identification through proposal development, negotiation, and close.
- Collaborate with RSM client service teams to identify cross-functional and cross-selling opportunities across ERP, risk, compliance, cybersecurity, and transformation services.
- Develop and execute market strategies that expand RSM's presence in FDA-regulated industries.
- Represent RSM at industry events, conferences, and client roundtables to enhance brand recognition and generate pipeline opportunities.
- Act as a trusted advisor to client executives by helping them understand business, operational, and regulatory risks associated with ERP transformation programs.
- Maintain and grow a healthy sales pipeline while achieving individual and practice revenue goals.

Responsibilities:
- Lead a cross‑functional team of subject‑matter experts spanning: Governance & compliance, Risk management, Application security, Data governance, IT controls FDA validation & assurance
- Develop and expand market-leading service offerings focused on ERP transformation risk, FDA CSA/CSV validation readiness, system integrity, compliance, and business process controls within life sciences organizations.
- Ensure application design decisions (configuration, integrations, data model, workflows) incorporate necessary regulatory requirements, compliance, traceability, and control requirements.
- Review and approve solution designs to ensure alignment with GxP boundaries, regulated vs. non‑regulated process flows, and required IT controls.
- Establish and manage program‑wide governance frameworks that ensure integrity, traceability, and compliance throughout the full implementation lifecycle.
- Drive resolution of regulatory and compliance issues, serving as the escalation point for solution design, validation, or control gaps.
- Ensure quality of all client deliverables created by the technical SMEs, including risk logs, assessment reports, mitigation plans, design documentation, and testing packages.
- Direct the creation of governance models, risk and control matrices, access control strategies, and data integrity safeguards across ERP platforms.
- Lead, mentor, and grow a multidisciplinary team of solution engineers, validation SMEs, GRC specialists, security architects, and data governance professionals.
- Build and mature internal methodologies, accelerators, templates, and best practices to enhance delivery consistency and efficiency.

- Help shape RSM's go-to-market strategy for regulatory compliance and ERP transformation services, identifying emerging client needs, industry trends, and growth opportunities.

- Identify and drive new business opportunities through demonstrating value.
- Accountable for engagement contracting, financials, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting, to ensure profitability.
- Effectively communicate program risk to key stake holders along with mitigating solutions across the enterprise and aid in managing resistance through the ability to communicate value and awareness.

jobs.description:

The Treasury Manager is responsible for overseeing the firm’s global daily cash-management activities, ensuring sufficient liquidity to meet operational and financial obligations while optimizing available cash.

This role manages daily cash positioning, cash-flow forecasting, banking activities, payments, short-term investments and borrowing, bank relationships, treasury accounting, and general ledger activities. The Cash Manager will collaborate with Accounting, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, FP&A, Tax, and business leaders to improve cash visibility, maintain accurate financial records, and support liquidity decisions.

Location:
Chicago or New York City - Hybrid

Key Responsibilities
Daily cash and Liquidity Management
- Manage daily cash positioning across the firm’s bank accounts and legal entities
- Monitor cash balances, inflows, outflows, and upcoming funding requirements
- Ensure sufficient liquidity is available to meet payroll, vendor payments, tax payments, debt obligations, and other operational requirements
- Initiate or coordinate intercompany and interbank transfers to efficiently concentrate and deploy cash
- Manage and monitor the daily flows of the cash pooling structure across multiple bank partners
- Optimize the use of excess cash, including short-term investments or debt repayment, in accordance with the firm’s policy
- Monitor available credit facilities and coordinate short-term borrowings when necessary
- Identify opportunities to reduce idle cash, avoid unnecessary borrowing, and improve working-capital efficiency
- Oversee daily banking activities, including cash administration, payments, collections, funding, and account management
- Review and approve wire transfers, ACH payments, and other non-routine transactions in accordance with delegated authority
- Manage bank accounts, authorized signers, account documentation, and online banking access

Cash-Flow Forecasting and Reporting
- Prepare and maintain short- and medium-term cash-flow forecasts in the CFF platform including daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly liquidity projections
- Partner with FP&A, Accounting, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Tax, Payroll to collect and validate forecast inputs.
- Analyze actual cash flows against forecasts and explain material variances
- Identify potential liquidity surpluses or shortfalls and recommend appropriate actions

Treasury Accounting and General Ledger
- Oversee the accurate and timely recording of cash transactions in the general ledger

- Award set-up & maintenance. Set up and maintain awards in the client's system — award terms, period of performance, budget lines, funder codes, restriction classification and billing basis.
- Transaction processing. Process grant-coded transactions: allocations of payroll, fringe and shared costs; grant-specific AP/AR; journal entries; cost transfers with documented justification; and monthly reconciliation of grant receivables, deferred revenue and net asset balances.
- Reporting & billing. Prepare funder financial reports and invoices across federal, state, local, foundation and corporate templates. Prepare drawdown and reimbursement requests through the applicable funder portals and reconcile them to the general ledger.
- Compliance monitoring. Test costs against the allowable, allocable and reasonable standard, monitor budget versus actual by line, flag over-runs, expiring funds and unallowable costs, and track prior-approval and budget-modification triggers before they become findings.
- Indirect cost recovery. Apply the client's negotiated or de minimis indirect cost rate, calculate the applicable cost base correctly, and reconcile recovered indirect costs each period.
- Subrecipient support. Support subrecipient monitoring — invoice review, eligibility and exclusion checks, risk assessment documentation and the related transparency filings.
- Audit & filing support. Prepare grant-related audit schedules and supporting documentation, respond to auditor queries, and support annual regulatory and information-return filings.
- Cross-functional coordination. Act as the India-side point of contact for client programme managers, development and fundraising teams, HR-payroll and the US engagement team — chasing documentation, resolving coding queries, running status calls and escalating early.
- Process & review. Maintain grant trackers, close checklists and desktop procedures; identify automation and standardisation opportunities; review the work of Associates and support their on-the-job training.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- CA / CPA / CMA / MBA (Finance) or B.Com with equivalent depth; 4–7 years in accounting, of which at least 2–3 years must be in a not-for-profit environment. Not-for-profit experience is essential; it may have been gained with Indian or US organisations.
- Working command of of U.S. GAAP for Not-for-Profit entities (ASC 958), including donor-restricted and without-donor-restriction net assets, contribution and grant accounting (ASU 2018-08), contributed nonfinancial assets (ASU 2020-07), ASC 606 revenue recognition.
- Experience with grant cost allocation methodologies and time-and-effort / payroll certification requirements.
- Fund accounting proficiency in at least one platform — Sage Intacct, Blackbaud Financial Edge NXT, MIP Fund Accounting, NetSuite or Workday; advanced Excel (pivots, lookups, large-file reconciliation).
- Clear written and spoken English, comfortable holding independent conversations with US-based client stakeholders.
- Willingness to work the 2:00 PM – 11:00 PM IST shift on a sustained basis, with flexibility during month-end, funder deadlines and audit season.

PREFERRED

- Experience supporting US-based clients or stakeholders from an offshore or shared-services location.
- Familiarity with grants management tools and reporting/automation tools (Power BI, Alteryx, Power Query).
- Exposure to grant proposal budgeting, award close-out and carryforward analysis.

jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Role Purpose
The India Procurement Lead owns end-to-end procurement governance for the indirect and corporate spending of RSM US Integrated. The role will be responsible for ensuring that procurement is conducted through a consistent, transparent and commercially rigorous enterprise framework, aligned with RSM’s global procurement policies, standards and category strategies while appropriately reflecting India business, regulatory and market requirements.

Working closely with business and functional leaders across India, the Procurement Lead will help translate business requirements into effective sourcing strategies, identify opportunities for commercial optimization, manage supplier and contracting processes, and strengthen procurement governance and supplier performance.

This role is the single point of accountability for ensuring every India purchase is sourced against the right vendor, at the right price, and to the right quality standard, while staying inside the enterprise procurement framework. The role sits at the intersection of commercial efficiency and control. The Procurement Lead is expected to operate as a business partner to department heads across the firm, and as the India voice into global category strategy.

Key Responsibilities
1. Purchase Governance and Value Delivery
- Lead sourcing decision, vendor selection, and negotiated price for India procurement within a defined threshold for various segments, including but not limited to facilities, IT, travel, professional services, marketing, admin, and talent.

- Validate vendor selection is competitively and commercially justified, price is benchmarked against market or prior contract terms, and quality/service specification meets the requesting department's stated need.

- Promote an enterprise-wide approach to procurement, reducing fragmented or function-specific buying where aggregation can create better commercial or service outcomes.

2. Category Management and Sourcing
- Develop forward procurement pipelines with major functions to improve planning and reduce reactive or urgent sourcing.

- Run competitive sourcing (RFI/RFP/RFQ) for new vendor requirements above a defined value threshold; negotiate commercial terms directly for categories owned locally.

- Determine the appropriate sourcing route, including competitive tender, global agreement, preferred supplier, single-source or justified exception.

- Maintain a rolling savings and cost avoidance tracker, reported monthly to India leadership.

- Periodically benchmark material categories and contracts against market practices and available alternatives.

3. Global Alignment and Coordination
- Operate within the enterprise procurement policy, DOA framework, and approved vendor/supplier standards; do not create exceptions without sign-off from relevant stakeholders.

- Own India demand aggregation for globally negotiated categories: consolidate India requirements and feed them into global category planning cycles and negotiations, providing India-specific demand, supplier, pricing and market inputs.

- Monitor India's utilization and compliance against global contracts and negotiated agreements, and for purchases under global contracts, confirm the India entity has appropriate contractual coverage and that local requirements are addressed.

- Serve as India's representative in global procurement forums, surfacing India-specific constraints (regulatory, vendor landscape, currency) that global procurement strategy needs to account for.

- Escalate circumstances where global arrangements do not adequately meet India commercial, regulatory, or operational requirements.

4. Stakeholder Management
- Act as the single point of contact for functional heads raising procurement needs, translating business requirements into a compliant sourcing process without adding unnecessary friction.

- Provide stakeholders with market intelligence, supplier insights, commercial benchmarks and sourcing recommendations.

- Challenge and refine requirements where appropriate to improve commercial outcomes, avoid unnecessary spend or identify alternative solutions.

- Set and manage service level expectations with internal stakeholders for sourcing turnaround time, distinguishing standard requisitions from urgent/exception requests.

5. Vendor and Supplier Management & Contracting
- Establish a risk- and value-based supplier segmentation framework for India.

- Maintain the India approved vendor list, including onboarding due diligence (financial health, compliance checks, data security posture where relevant).

- Establish supplier KPIs, SLAs and performance-review mechanisms in partnership with business owners.

- Work closely with Legal, Finance, Information Security, Risk, Privacy and relevant business owners to coordinate the commercial contracting process.

- Ensure material supplier arrangements are appropriately documented through contracts, statements of work, purchase orders or other approved instruments.

- Establish a structured contract-renewal process to prevent automatic or poorly negotiated renewals.

- Facilitate appropriate commercial review of contract amendments, extensions and scope changes.

6. Compliance, Risk, and Reporting
- As custodian of the India procurement policy and framework, ensure all India procurement activity complies with enterprise policy, statutory requirements (GST, TDS, contract law as applicable), and any independence rules relevant to vendor selection.

- Produce a monthly procurement governance report to the India Country Leader and India Finance Leader.

- Maintain visibility of procurement exceptions, non-compliant spend and retrospective procurement activity, and drive corrective actions.

- Maintain an auditable trail for every sourcing decision (vendor comparison, price rationale, approval record) sufficient to withstand internal audit and control testing.

- Support internal audits, statutory reviews and other assurance activities relating to procurement and vendors.

Required Experience and Qualifications
- 14+ years in procurement, sourcing, or category management, with at least 3 to 5 years in an India GCC, shared services, or professional services environment.

- Demonstrated ownership of an approval/sign-off process, not just sourcing execution; experience operating within a formal framework.

- Working knowledge of indirect procurement categories: facilities, IT, travel, marketing, etc.

- Experience coordinating with a global or centralized procurement function while managing local execution; comfort operating in a dual accountability structure.

- Familiarity with P2P systems (Ariba, Coupa, or equivalent) and audit/control expectations (SOX/ICFR exposure is a plus).

- Strong stakeholder management skills; ability to hold a firm line on policy and price with senior internal stakeholders without becoming an obstacle to the business.

jobs.title: Learning and Development Business Partner Director (Location Flexible)
jobs.description:

The Learning & Development Business Partner Director serves as the senior strategic learning and capability advisor to an assigned line of business and their leaders. The Director translates business, workforce, and talent priorities into an integrated capability strategy that improves business performance, strengthens professional readiness, and advances RSM's First Choice Advisor strategy. The Director is a key leader in the ongoing evolution of the Learning & Development function, helping shape operating models, workforce capability strategies, service delivery approaches, and learning technology adoption to ensure the organization can meet future business needs.

As a member of the L&D leadership team, the Director provides thought leadership, cultivates line of business and enterprise-wide relationships, and leads large, complex initiatives with significant business impact. The role works across L&D and Talent to mobilize the right expertise, scale effective solutions, and create appropriate consistency across the firm while remaining responsive to distinct business needs.

Key Responsibilities
Business and Capability Strategy
- Build trusted relationships with senior business and talent leaders and serve as a first-choice advisor on workforce capability, performance, and development priorities.

- Translate firm, talent, and business strategies into multi-year capability roadmaps with clear priorities, outcomes, measures, investment requirements, and decision points.

- Use performance consulting and systems thinking to distinguish capability needs from process, role clarity, technology, capacity, leadership, or other performance barriers.

- Proactively identify emerging capability risks and opportunities based on business plans, workforce trends, client needs, professional standards, and changes in the market.

- Influence leaders to make disciplined choices among competing needs and focus resources on the work most likely to improve business and talent outcomes.

- Advise on the appropriate mix of education, experience, exposure, environment, performance support, coaching, knowledge resources, communities, and technology-enabled approaches.

Organizational Transformation and Change Leadership
- Act as a visible champion of the firm's learning and capability transformation strategy.

- Drive adoption of new operating models, workflows, roles, governance structures, and technologies.

- Challenge legacy processes and approaches that no longer create sufficient business value.

- Influence leaders to embrace scalable, data-informed approaches to capability development.

- Balance immediate business demands with long-term organizational capability building.

- Lead change efforts that require stakeholder alignment across service lines, Talent, Learning Operations, Talent Technology, and other shared services.

- Identify organizational barriers to transformation and proactively develop mitigation strategies.

- Build change readiness among stakeholders and teams impacted by evolving learning strategies and operating models.

Portfolio and Investment Leadership
- Own the strategic portfolio of capability investments for the assigned business, ensuring solutions are connected, sequenced, scalable, and aligned to role and career expectations.
- Establish priorities and governance for major capability initiatives, including sponsorship, decision rights, measures, dependencies, and escalation paths.
- Oversee the business partner budget and recommend resource and investment trade-offs using evidence, expected impact, and enterprise priorities.

- Identify opportunities to reuse and scale effective solutions across service lines while allowing appropriate flexibility for distinct business needs.

Solution Leadership and Cross-Functional Partnership
- Frame the business problem, target audience, desired performance, success measures, and constraints before solution design begins.

- Mobilize and guide cross-functional teams that may include learning architects, strategic learning advisors, experience delivery, Learning Operations, Talent Technology, communications, change, and external partners.
- Communicate strategy, progress, decisions, risks, and required actions clearly to stakeholders at all levels.

Measurement, Impact, and Continuous Improvement
- Define financial and non-financial measures that connect capability investments to intended business, talent, learner, adoption, and performance outcomes.

- Use data and stakeholder evidence to evaluate impact, test assumptions, identify barriers to transfer, and adjust the portfolio.

- Provide leaders with a clear view of investment performance, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations for continuation, redesign, expansion, or retirement.

- Promote disciplined experimentation and the responsible adoption of new methods and technologies that improve access, speed, quality, personalization, or impact.

- Capture, share, and scale leading practices across L&D and the broader Talent function.

Enterprise and L&D Leadership
- Act as a critical member of the L&D leadership team, contributing to enterprise strategy, operating priorities, governance, and organizational performance.

- Lead or sponsor enterprise initiatives that advance firm, Talent, and L&D strategies and require coordination across businesses, functions, or geographies.

- Champion the modernization of learning through clearer roles, integrated workflows, stronger capability consulting, improved measurement, and effective use of technology.

- Balance the priorities of the assigned business with enterprise needs and actively challenge siloed approaches.

- Lead through ambiguity and change, surface difficult issues, and facilitate timely decisions with senior stakeholders.

- Model RSM's 5 C behaviors by being caring, collaborative, courageous, curious, and an exemplary critical thinker.

People Leadership
- Build and develop a high-performing, inclusive team of learning professionals with clear expectations, accountability, and connection to business outcomes.

- Serve as a performance advisor to Managers and/or Associate Directors, consistent with business need and organizational design.

- Delegate meaningful and challenging work, provide timely and direct feedback, address performance gaps, and support career development and succession.

- Develop the team's business acumen, consulting capability, learning expertise, change leadership, and data fluency.

- Create an environment that encourages thoughtful challenge, collaboration, continuous learning, and responsible innovation.

Required Qualifications
Education and Experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience required; advanced degree in learning, organizational development, business, talent management, or a related field preferred.

- Typically 12+ years of overall experience, with significant relevant experience in learning and development, capability building, performance consulting, organizational effectiveness, talent, or a related discipline. Role relevance, complexity, scope, and demonstrated impact are more important than tenure alone.

- Demonstrated success developing strategies that impact business performance and leading large-scale, global, complex, or enterprise-wide initiatives.

- Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders, maintaining key internal client relationships, and navigating sensitive or high-impact business matters.

- Experience leading professional teams and serving as a performance advisor to experienced people leaders.

- Experience in professional services, public accounting, consulting, or another complex, regulated, or knowledge-intensive environment preferred.

- Knowledge of Assurance, Tax, Consulting, or Firm Client Service business models is preferred. CPA or other relevant professional certification is a plus.

Business, Consulting, and Leadership Capabilities
- Strategic and systems thinking, with the ability to connect business strategy, workforce needs, talent practices, and capability investments.

- Executive-level consulting, influence, facilitation, and communication skills, including the courage to challenge assumptions and recommend trade-offs.

- Deep knowledge of adult learning, performance consulting, capability development, instructional design, assessment, transfer of learning, and evaluation.

- Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to diagnose needs, establish measures, and communicate business impact.

- Ability to lead through ambiguity, manage risk, resolve complex issues, and adapt priorities while maintaining focus on outcomes.

- Ability to lead across organizational boundaries and align stakeholders who have different priorities, perspectives, or levels of authority.

- Financial and portfolio management capability, including budgeting, investment prioritization, resource decisions, and vendor oversight.

- Working knowledge of learning technology, digital learning, performance support, knowledge enablement, and emerging approaches that may improve capability outcomes.

- Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, Excel, SharePoint, and other tools needed to analyze, communicate, and manage strategic work.

Success in This Role
- Business leaders view L&D as a trusted advisor and involve the Director early in strategic workforce and capability decisions.

- Capability investments are clearly prioritized, connected to business needs, and supported by meaningful measures of adoption, performance, and impact.

- L&D expertise is mobilized effectively, with clear ownership across strategy, design, delivery, operations, technology, and measurement.

- Effective solutions and practices are scaled across the enterprise while distinct business needs are addressed thoughtfully.

- The Director develops strong leaders and teams and contributes materially to the performance and modernization of the broader L&D function.

- Learning investments increasingly demonstrate measurable business impact.

The Security Operations Analyst is responsible for detecting, investigating, and responding to cybersecurity threats and incidents across the organization’s systems, networks, cloud environments, and applications. This role helps protect enterprise assets by monitoring security controls, leading incident investigations, coordinating response activities, and driving continuous improvement of threat and vulnerability management programs.

The analyst applies structured analytical techniques to assess risk, identify emerging threats, and provide actionable recommendations to Information Technology and business leadership. The role also contributes to broader Information Security initiatives, including security architecture reviews, standards development, security automation, and operational maturity improvements.

Key Responsibilities

Security Monitoring and Incident Response

- Monitor security events and alerts across enterprise technologies to identify malicious activity, security incidents, and control failures.

- Investigate cybersecurity events and incidents, including malware infections, account compromise, insider threats, phishing attacks, unauthorized access attempts, and data security concerns.

- Coordinate and facilitate incident response activities across technical and business teams.

- Execute containment, eradication, and recovery activities during security incidents.

- Perform root cause analysis and document lessons learned following incident resolution.

- Maintain incident documentation, evidence collection, and reporting in accordance with organizational standards.

Threat Detection and Threat Management

- Monitor for attempts to circumvent security controls by internal users, third parties, and external threat actors.

- Conduct threat hunting activities using available telemetry, logs, and threat intelligence.

- Manage and improve security detection capabilities within SIEM, EDR, and related security technologies.

- Analyze threat intelligence and translate findings into actionable security improvements.

- Maintain blacklist, watchlist, and detection management processes.

Vulnerability Management

- Execute and continuously improve vulnerability management processes across infrastructure, applications, cloud environments, and emerging technologies.

- Coordinate vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, secure code reviews, red team exercises, and remediation efforts.

- Evaluate vulnerabilities for business risk and prioritize remediation activities.

- Track remediation progress and communicate risk exposure to leadership and stakeholders.

Security Operations and Continuous Improvement

- Analyze, evaluate, and test the effectiveness of existing security controls.

- Assess security processes and identify opportunities for operational improvement and increased efficiency.

- Apply structured analytical methodologies to incident investigations, threat analysis, and process optimization efforts.

- Develop operational metrics, reporting, and dashboards to support risk-informed decision-making.

- Support audit, compliance, and regulatory initiatives as required .

Security Strategy and Collaboration

- Communicate security risks, control effectiveness, and incident trends to Information Technology leadership and business stakeholders.

- Support security architecture reviews, technology evaluations, and project security assessments.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of security standards, policies, procedures, and playbooks.

- Partner with infrastructure, cloud, application development, and business teams to strengthen the organization’s overall security posture.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

- Five or more years of experience in cybersecurity, security operations, incident response, or threat management.

- Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams during cybersecurity incidents.

- Strong understanding of security principles across operating systems, applications, networking, cloud platforms, mobile technologies, endpoint security, and identity and access management.

- Experience with SIEM, EDR/XDR, vulnerability management, and security monitoring technologies.

- Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to perform effectively under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

- Industry certifications such as CISSP, GCIH, GCFA, CISA, CEH, OSCP, or Security+.

- Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Computer Science, or related discipline.

- Experience managing or responding to significant cybersecurity incidents and enterprise-scale investigations.

- Experience with business intelligence, reporting, and data analytics tools.

- Experience with Python, PowerShell, or other automation and orchestration technologies.

- Experience designing or supporting Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) solutions.

- Knowledge of threat intelligence, digital forensics, cloud-native security , and modern detection engineering practices.

- Experience applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, or neural network technologies to cybersecurity operations.

- Team management/People experience.
- Understanding of financial statements, financial ratio analysis, U.S. GAAP accounting standards, financial concepts, etc.

jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

The Information Security Governance Analyst is responsible for multiple information security-governance, risk, and compliance- related activities. This includes reviewing the security posture of vendors, coordination of information security audit activities, supporting and client due diligence by responding to client security questionnaires, requests for proposal, and requests for information. Responsibilities include managing information security program and security awareness documentation and content.
Essential Duties
- Audit & Assessment Liaison Activities: Liaise, plan and coordinate information security audits including coordination with auditors and control owners. Liaise with auditors to gather and evaluate evidence for information security audits, drive remediation efforts and report on potential risks. Conduct mock-audits and control reviews. Communicates the effectiveness of security controls to leadership.
- Perform Vendor Due Diligence: Review the security posture of vendors and third parties. This includes reviewing responses to vendor security questionnaires, writing assessment reports, and communicating risks to the Line of Business contacts.
- Provide Client Due Diligence Support: Respond to and complete client security questionnaires, requests for proposal, and requests for information.
- Manage Information Security Program Documentation: Review and update information security policy, standards, procedures and related documentation. Provide subject matter expertise in the areas of security policies, standards and related compliance.
- Manage Security Awareness Content: Manage phishing tests, coordinate updates to security awareness course content, periodic articles and report / escalate delinquencies.

Minimum Qualifications
EDUCATION/CERTIFICATIONS
Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in cyber security, information systems, or related field or equivalent level of experience

TECHNICAL/SOFT SKILLS
Required:
- Critical and structured thinking, formal analytic methods
- Solid understanding of security applied to OS, applications, networking, cloud, mobile, etc.
- Ability to perform under pressure and handle multiple priorities
- Ability to self-motivate and work independently
- Strong organizational skills

EXPERIENCE
Required:
- 2+ years information security experience
- 1+ years experience performing vendor security assessments / vendor due diligence

Preferred
- Experience responding to client due diligence inquiries

COMMUNICATION SKILLS
Required:
- Required: Excellent written and oral communication
- Preferred: Ability to translate technical terms into layman’s terms
